channel.title: CounselO Global Legal Insights
channel.description: Legal articles and guides covering UAE, Saudi and Syrian law.

item.title: The 5Why Methodology in Legal Practice
item.description: The "5Why" methodology in legal practice: How does it uncover the real cause behind losing cases and disputes? In legal practice many believe the loss stems from the court ruling or weak advocacy, but experience shows the judgment is often the result of a chain...

item.title: Subject Matter of a Contract under Syrian Law
item.description: The subject matter of a contract under Syrian law, its requirements, and how their absence affects validity. A valid contract requires more than mutual consent: the agreed performance must be legally recognizable and capable of producing binding effects.

item.title: Terminating an Employment Contract Without Lawful Cause
item.description: When does termination without lawful cause constitute unfair dismissal? This article explains potentially unlawful termination under Saudi Labor Law, the distinction between lawful termination and unfair dismissal, and the rights and procedures that help workers protect their legal position.

item.title: Delayed Wages or Non-Payment
item.description: Delayed wages or non-payment: procedures and rights under Saudi law. Wages are a core element of the employment relationship, and any delay or refusal to pay may affect a worker's fundamental right and require a clear legal response according to the circumstances of the case.

item.title: Contractual Capacity under Syrian Law
item.description: Contractual capacity under Syrian law: who may conclude a contract, and how does a lack of capacity affect its validity? Consent, a lawful object, and a lawful cause are not enough; the intention must also come from a person with legal capacity to undertake the transaction.

item.title: Risk Management in Contracts Under Saudi Law
item.description: Risk management in commercial contracts under Saudi law provides a practical framework for protecting parties and reducing disputes.

item.title: Practical Recommendations for Drafting a Strong Contract
item.description: Practical recommendations for drafting a strong contract under the Saudi legal system: a comprehensive guide for lawyers and commercial parties. Contract drafting is a fundamental step in any commercial or civil relationship, defining the parties’ rights and obligations and serving as the primary reference in the event of a dispute.

item.title: Consent in Syrian Law
item.description: Consent in Syrian law: offer, acceptance, and how a contract is formed. Consent is the cornerstone of contract theory and the basis from which all contractual relationships arise.

item.title: Contracts in Syrian Law
item.description: Contracts in Syrian law: concept, elements, characteristics, and practical importance. This introductory article explains contract theory in Syrian law in language that combines legal precision with practical clarity, focusing on the general concept of the contract and its characteristics.

item.title: Proving Contracts Before the Saudi Courts
item.description: Proving contracts before the Saudi courts: evidence, presumptions, the evidentiary value of documents, and digital evidence. Proving contracts is among the most important stages of litigation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as the judge bases the ruling on the evidence presented, not on personal knowledge. With the issuance of the Evidence Law...

item.title: Commercial Franchise Agreements in the Saudi Legal System
item.description: Commercial franchise agreements in the Saudi legal system: regulatory controls and practical risks. Franchise agreements have become among the most important commercial tools in the Saudi market.

item.title: Compensation for Breach of Contract under Syrian Law
item.description: An overview of the conditions, scope, and judicial assessment of compensation for breach of contract under Syrian law.

item.title: Commercial Agency Contracts in the Saudi Legal System
item.description: Commercial agency contracts in Saudi Arabia: the rights and responsibilities of agents and principals.

item.title: Construction Contracts under Saudi Law
item.description: Construction contracts under Saudi law: mutual obligations, liability, and performance disputes.

item.title: Contractual Liability under Syrian Law
item.description: When is a contracting party liable for breaching a contract under Syrian law? This article outlines the requirements, effects, and remedies of contractual liability.

item.title: Performance of Contracts in Good Faith under Syrian Law
item.description: Good-faith performance of contracts under Syrian law is a legal safeguard for transactional stability and contractual justice, turning written obligations into fair conduct between the parties.

item.title: Commercial Supply Contracts in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Commercial supply contracts in Saudi Arabia: key legal clauses and the risks of breach.

item.title: Electronic Contracts in the Saudi Legal System
item.description: Electronic contracts have become a commercial and regulatory reality that cannot be ignored. Saudi law grants them recognised evidentiary value when their elements and requirements are satisfied and they can be attributed to and verified against their parties. The more thoroughly the data are documented, identities authenticated, and records securely preserved, the stronger the electronic contract becomes before the courts and the less likely disputes are over its validity or attribution to its parties.

item.title: Contract Interpretation Before Syrian Courts
item.description: Contract interpretation before Syrian courts seeks the parties' true common intention through clarity, good faith, custom, and the nature of the transaction.

item.title: Consensual, Formal, and Real Contracts in Syrian Law
item.description: Syrian law distinguishes between consensual, formal, and real contracts because each type has different requirements for formation and legal effect.

item.title: Termination of Commercial Contracts under Saudi Law
item.description: An overview of the conditions, effects, and methods of proving termination of commercial contracts under Saudi law, particularly in supply, construction, and service disputes.

item.title: Defects of Consent in Syrian Law: Mistake, Duress, Fraud, and Exploitation
item.description: Free will and sound consent are fundamental to contracts under Syrian civil law. A contract may be rescinded where consent is impaired by mistake, duress, fraud, or exploitation.

item.title: Formation of Commercial Contracts Under Saudi Law
item.description: Learn the essential elements, validity requirements, formation stages, and legal consequences of commercial contracts under Saudi law.

item.title: Penalty Clauses in Commercial Contracts
item.description: A penalty clause is not merely an additional contract term.

item.title: Contractual Liability in Commercial Transactions
item.description: A legal overview of contractual liability in Saudi commercial transactions, including its conditions, forms of breach, compensation, penalty clauses, and risk mitigation.
